source: Jawaharlal Nehru Port Authority via Maritime Gateway (2025): record 7.3 million TEU in FY 2024-25 (+13.55%), of which 1,078,315 TEU moved by rail. Transshipment share: JNPT is a gateway port with little transshipment (calibrated). Road share: the published rail volume is 14.8% of throughput, so road carries about 85% of hinterland boxes.
circuity_check: Mumbai-Pune Expressway, Kalamboli to Kiwale: published 94.5 km against a 79.0 km great-circle separation (circuity 1.196)

source: Administracion del Sistema Portuario Nacional Manzanillo via Mexico Business News, 3,893,357 TEU in 2025 Transshipment share: Manzanillo is predominantly a gateway port with some coastal relay. The road share is applied to hinterland (non-transshipment) throughput only; both the transshipment and road shares are calibrated and are varied in the sensitivity analysis.
circuity_check: Manzanillo Port to Guadalajara via MEX-54D: derived 311.5 km vs published ~310 km

source: Port of Rotterdam 2025 throughput: 14.2 M TEU (+3.1%), 428.4 Mt total cargo (-1.7%) Transshipment share: About 30% of Rotterdam container throughput is transshipment that never touches a road. The road share is applied to hinterland (non-transshipment) throughput only; both the transshipment and road shares are calibrated and are varied in the sensitivity analysis.
circuity_check: Maasvlakte to Venlo via A15/A16/A58/A67: derived 187.0 km vs published ~180 km

source: Port of Los Angeles, Container Statistics 2025: 10,239,318 TEU in calendar 2025 (loaded imports 5,316,713; loaded exports 1,429,260; empties 3,493,344). Transshipment: negligible. Road share: the share not moved by on-dock or near-dock rail is calibrated at 0.70 (not published at this resolution) and varied in the sensitivity analysis. Truck TEU factor reflects the predominance of 40-ft boxes (calibrated).
circuity_check: Los Angeles to Las Vegas by I-15: published about 435 km against a 367.6 km great-circle separation (circuity 1.18)

source: Port of Shanghai via Container News (2026): 55.06 million TEU in 2025 (+6.9%), of which international transshipment 7.911 million TEU (14.4%) and sea-rail 1 million TEU. Road share: a large share of hinterland boxes moves by Yangtze and canal barge; the road share of non-transshipment throughput is calibrated at 0.45 (not published) and varied in the sensitivity analysis. Port node placed at Waigaoqiao; about half of volume is handled at Yangshan.
circuity_check: G42 Shanghai-Nanjing (Huning) Expressway: 274 km between its termini at Zhenru (Shanghai) and Maqun (Nanjing), about 250 km apart on a great circle (circuity 1.10, the value used)

source: DP World FY2025 results: Jebel Ali handled 15.6 million TEU in 2025 (+0.1%). Transshipment share: Jebel Ali is a major Gulf transshipment hub; the share is calibrated at 0.50 (not published) and varied in the sensitivity analysis. Road share: almost all hinterland boxes move by road (calibrated 0.95).
circuity_check: Dubai to Abu Dhabi by E11: published about 140 km against a 122.9 km great-circle separation (circuity 1.14)

source: Busan Port Authority via Kuehne+Nagel (2026): 24.8 million TEU in 2025 (+2%), of which transshipment 14.1 million TEU (57%). Road share of gateway boxes calibrated at 0.92 (rail and coastal shipping carry the rest; not published at this resolution) and varied in the sensitivity analysis. Port node placed at Busan New Port.
circuity_check: Gyeongbu Expressway, Seoul to Busan: 416 km against about 310-315 km between its termini on a great circle (circuity 1.32-1.34); 1.30 is used, so derived lengths on this corridor may be up to about 3% short

source: Derived: Transnet Port Terminals handled 4,091,718 TEU nationally in FY 2024/25 (Transnet Port Terminals 2025 performance report). The Port of Durban handles over 60% of South Africa's container volume (Transnet; BusinessDay, 13 May 2026); a share of 0.65 is applied, giving 0.65 x 4,091,718 = 2,659,617 TEU. The share is calibrated, not published at this resolution (the 65% figure Transnet publishes is the Durban Container Terminal's share of the port's own throughput). Transshipment (0.10) and road share (0.85) are calibrated and varied in the sensitivity analysis.
circuity_check: Durban to Johannesburg by the N3: published about 568-578 km against a 500.3 km great-circle separation (circuity 1.14-1.16; 1.14 used)
